meta.style: Painted digital illustration, west coast of Scotland, late August, low grey Atlantic light with one warm amber lamp in frame, slate-blue sea, wet black granite, kelp green and rust red, soft brush edges, no hard outlines, eye-level three-quarter camera

inspiration.title: Jaws
inspiration.author: Steven Spielberg
inspiration.adaptation: Original west-coast-of-Scotland adaptation of the closed-beach premise, with a kraken.

cover.eyebrow: PRESENT PERFECT + CONTINUOUS - WEST HIGHLAND RPG
cover.title: KRAKEN: THE BLACK TIDE
cover.lead: You are Sergeant Isla Brodie, new to Kilmara and no friend of deep water. Two creel boats went out and their crews are still out there. The Provost will not close the water.
cover.small: Single player · B1 · eighteen questions · two branching routes

briefing.title: YOUR PERFECT TENSES SEA CHART

cards.head: FORM · HAVE / HAS + PAST PARTICIPLE
cards.text: The village HAS heard nothing YET, and the crews HAVE NOT returned.

cards.head: FORM · HAVE / HAS + BEEN + -ING
cards.text: The gulls HAVE BEEN circling all morning: not BEING, not HAVE circling.

cards.head: A RESULT vs AN ACTIVITY
cards.text: Numbers are RESULTS: Baird HAS counted three boats. Visitors HAVE BEEN arriving.

cards.head: HOW LONG · HAVE + SUBJECT + BEEN + -ING?
cards.text: HOW LONG HAS Hoy BEEN listening? SINCE dawn, or FOR six hours.

cards.head: STATE VERBS REFUSE THE -ING
cards.text: Kilmara HAS wanted a lifeboat FOR years.

briefing.note: A finished time takes the PAST SIMPLE: the boat WENT out at six, two hours AGO.

hotspot.object: the yellow barrel in the stern

drift.title: A BOAT COMES BACK
drift.story: Dawn on the pier. A creel boat turns in the bay with its rope trailing. The seats are empty.
drift.clue: The yellow barrel in the stern hangs by a stub of rope. Both coats are aboard.
drift.prompt: What do you say to the men on the pier?
drift.explanation: Present Perfect for a past event with a result now: HAS + TAKEN. TOOK is Past Simple, and one sea takes HAS.

bell.title: ONE BERTH STAYS EMPTY
bell.story: You ring the harbour bell. Doors open along the street. Men count the boats at the pier, then count them again.
bell.clue: The brass bell rings over one empty space, and no engine answers from the Sound.
bell.prompt: What do you say when the ringing stops?
bell.explanation: The negative of the Present Perfect is HAVE NOT + COME. English never builds it with BE, and THEY takes HAVE.

provost.title: THE PROVOST SAYS NO
provost.story: Provost Baird will not close the water. Regatta Week starts tomorrow, and the whole village needs the money.
provost.clue: The red buoy stays out in the Sound, and no coastguard boat is in the bay.
provost.prompt: How do you ask Baird about the coastguard?
provost.explanation: A yes/no question puts HAVE first: HAVE + YOU + CALLED. HAVE always needs the participle, never CALL or CALLING.

hoy.title: THE WOMAN FROM OBAN
hoy.story: A car stops at the top of the slip. Dr. Maren Hoy carries a metal case down.
hoy.clue: The sonar case is new and unscratched, and she is younger than you expected.
hoy.prompt: What do you ask Dr. Hoy first?

answers.text: Have you ever dived in this loch?
Ever have you dived in this loch?
Have ever you dived in this loch?

hoy.explanation: EVER asks about any time up to now, and it sits between the subject and the participle: HAVE + YOU + EVER + DIVED.

jar.title: THE RING OF HORN
jar.story: Dr. Hoy holds a jar up to the lamp. Inside is a black ring of horn, cut from something's beak.
jar.clue: The black ring in the glass jar is heavier than it looks in her hand.
jar.prompt: What does Dr. Hoy say about the ring?

answers.text: I have not never hold one this big.
I have never held one this big.
I have never holded one this big.

jar.explanation: NEVER already means not at any time, so HAVE stays positive: HAVE NEVER + HELD. HOLD is irregular and its participle is HELD.

hotspot.object: the yellow barrel on the wall

shed.title: QUINN OPENS HIS SHED
shed.story: Angus Quinn opens his shed. Yellow marker barrels hang along the wall. He turns one round, and you lift your radio.
shed.clue: The yellow barrel on the wall is bitten clean through the middle, and still swinging.
shed.prompt: What do you say into the radio?

answers.text: Quinn has found a bitten barrel just.
Quinn has just find a bitten barrel.
Quinn has just found a bitten barrel.

shed.explanation: JUST means a moment ago and goes between HAS and the participle: HAS + JUST + FOUND. It cannot sit at the end.

reef1.title: SHAPES ON THE SCREEN
reef1.story: Hoy swings her sonar float over the reef. Quinn cuts the engine. Shapes crowd the screen at once.
reef1.clue: The orange sonar float is barely wet, and the screen is full of moving shapes.
reef1.prompt: Hoy ___ the shapes on her sonar screen.
reef1.explanation: ALREADY goes between HAS and MARKED. HAS needs the participle MARKED, and one person takes HAS, not HAVE.

cave1.title: THE MOUTH AT LOW WATER
cave1.story: You and Hoy take the inflatable under the headland at low water. The roof drops to a hand above you.
cave1.clue: The storm lantern shows wet oar marks on the rock, and Quinn's boat is gone.
cave1.prompt: Quinn ___ into the cave ahead of you.
cave1.explanation: ALREADY sits between HAS and the participle ROWED. HAS never takes the bare ROW, and one man takes HAS.

reef2.title: CUT EDGE TO EDGE
reef2.story: Hoy pulls a creel net over the rail. It is cut through, edge to edge. Quinn turns it over.
reef2.clue: The torn net hangs on the rail. Quinn holds an end and looks at the water.
reef2.explanation: YET needs the Present Perfect negative: HAS NOT + SPOKEN. The Past Simple cannot take YET, and SPOKE is not the participle.

cave2.title: THE EMPTY DINGHY
cave2.story: Deep in the caves a dinghy lies over against the wall, half swamped. Water slaps the bare boards.
cave2.clue: The dinghy lamp burns on its hook, and both oars are still aboard.
cave2.prompt: The man who owns this dinghy ___ yet.
cave2.explanation: YET goes with the Present Perfect negative: HAS NOT + TURNED UP. DID and WAS cannot carry a participle here.

reef3.title: ONE SEAL LEFT
reef3.story: Quinn takes the Selkie past the low rocks. One seal on the whole rock. Hoy counts twice, then lowers the binoculars.
reef3.clue: The last seal lies alone on the rock, and Hoy's count comes to one.
reef3.prompt: The rest of the colony has been gone ___.
reef3.explanation: SINCE gives the point where it started: SINCE Monday morning. FOR needs a length of time, and ON cannot follow a Present Perfect.

cave3.title: SHELLS ON THE LEDGE
cave3.story: The passage opens into a chamber. Hoy lowers her sonar into the pool. The floor drops away under it.
cave3.clue: The broken creel on the ledge is Quinn's. He lost it on Tuesday, in calm water.
cave3.prompt: The broken creel up on the ledge ___.
cave3.explanation: SINCE gives the day it started: SINCE Tuesday. English needs HAS BEEN here, never IS here and never IS BEING here.

reef4.title: SOMETHING TOUCHES THE HULL
reef4.story: Something long drags down the side of the Selkie and is gone. Quinn keeps talking and turns for the old wreck.
reef4.clue: The scarred hull plate is raw wood. Quinn set his first creels here at fourteen.
reef4.prompt: What does Quinn say about his years on this water?

answers.text: I am still fishing here for forty years.
I have being fishing here for forty years.
I have been fishing here for forty years.

reef4.explanation: An activity running up to now takes HAVE + BEEN + -ING. The Present Continuous cannot reach back, and BEEN never becomes BEING.

cave4.title: THE CAVE IS FILLING
cave4.story: The cave is filling fast. Quinn is back aboard the inflatable, wet through. The mouth is still ahead of you.
cave4.clue: The wet tide line is overhead. The water was at your knees two hours ago.
cave4.prompt: What do you say about the water in here?

answers.text: The water has been rising since two hours.
The water has been rising for two hours.
The water has been rising two hours ago.

cave4.explanation: HAS + BEEN + -ING measures how long, and FOR marks the length. SINCE wants a starting point, and AGO wants the Past Simple.

hotspot.object: the yellow barrel rising in the water

wreck1.title: FOUR METRES OF WATER
wreck1.story: The Selkie stops over the Morag in four metres of water. Hoy goes over the side with a mask and comes up again.
wreck1.clue: A yellow barrel rises out of the wreck, and Hoy is back at the ladder.
wreck1.explanation: BEEN is there and back; GONE is still away. Hoy is at the ladder, so HAS BEEN. WENT is Past Simple, not the participle.

wreck2.title: THE SCAR ON HIS ARM
wreck2.story: Quinn rolls his sleeve back. The scar runs from wrist to elbow. The kraken marked him at twenty-six, and nobody believed him.
wreck2.clue: The old harpoon head in his hand is his own, and still sharp.
wreck2.prompt: How do you ask him about the hunt?

answers.text: How long you have been hunting it?
How long have you been hunting it?
How long have you being hunting it?

wreck2.explanation: HOW LONG asks for a duration, so the auxiliary moves in front of the subject. BEEN is fixed and never becomes BEING.

wreck3.title: TWENTY-EIGHT YEARS DOWN
wreck3.story: Quinn points down at the wreck. Twenty-eight years on the bottom, he says, and the village still will not say her name.
wreck3.clue: The brass porthole is scoured bright, and the hull plates below it are split open.
wreck3.explanation: A finished time forces the Past Simple: SANK in 1998. The Present Perfect never says WHEN, and the participle is SUNK.

corry1.title: A TURN ROUND THE DRUM
corry1.story: Quinn takes a turn round the iron drum. The Selkie leans over. Hoy braces herself against the wheelhouse door.
corry1.clue: Smoke comes off the rope on the iron drum. Quinn watches the islands.
corry1.prompt: What does Hoy say about Quinn and this water?

answers.text: He has known this water all his life.
He has been knowing this water all his life.
He knows this water all his life.

corry1.explanation: KNOW refuses the -ING, so a state takes HAS + KNOWN. A period reaching now needs HAS, not KNOWS.

night1.title: THE MOORED FLEET
night1.story: The regatta lights burn over the moored boats. Quinn told the fleet to stay in on Thursday, and every skipper is ashore.
night1.clue: The harbour lamp shows the whole fleet tied up on a Regatta Week night.
night1.prompt: Why is nobody out on the water tonight?

answers.text: They have been believing him since Thursday.
They all believe him since Thursday.
They have believed him since Thursday.

night1.explanation: Some verbs refuse the -ING: BELIEVE takes HAVE / HAS + PAST PARTICIPLE. A stretch of time up to now needs a perfect.

corry2.title: IT COMES UP
corry2.story: An arm comes up out of the sea and lies over the side. The rail bends under it. Hoy does not move.
corry2.clue: The arm over the side is thicker than a man and pale in the lamplight.
corry2.prompt: Quinn says it is the first time anyone ___.
corry2.explanation: After IT IS THE FIRST TIME English takes the Present Perfect: HAS + TOUCHED. HAD belongs to a past frame.

hotspot.object: the last lit lamp on the water

night2.title: ONE LAMP STILL BURNING
night2.story: One boat after another goes dark along the pontoon. Somewhere a halyard knocks. You count the lights down to one.
night2.clue: The last lit lamp on the water is a masthead light, small and white.
night2.prompt: Quinn says it is the first time the harbour ___ this dark.
night2.explanation: IT IS THE FIRST TIME takes the Present Perfect: HAS + BEEN. HAD belongs to a past frame, and HARBOUR is singular.

corry3.title: THE ENGINE STOPS
corry3.story: Quinn goes down to the engine. The Selkie loses way, and the Corry takes her round again.
corry3.clue: The engine lamp swings over the hot block. The note drops away as you listen.
corry3.prompt: What do you say to Hoy about the engine?

answers.text: It is still cutting out since dusk.
It cuts out again and again since dusk.
It has been cutting out since dusk.

corry3.explanation: An activity still running now takes HAS + BEEN + -ING. SINCE needs a perfect tense here, and never a present one.

night3.title: THE PONTOON LIFTS
night3.story: The pontoon lifts under your feet and drops back. The mooring rope comes up out of the black water.
night3.clue: The mooring rope is hard and tight. The steel cleat bent out of true after dark.
night3.prompt: What do you say as the rope comes up?

answers.text: Something is pulling it hard since dark.
Something pulls it tight since dark.
Something has been pulling it since dark.

night3.explanation: HAS + BEEN + -ING for something that began before now and has not stopped. SINCE marks where it began.

hotspot.object: the yellow barrel going over the rail

barrels.title: THE THIRD ONE GOES
barrels.story: Hoy swings the third barrel up onto the rail. The rope runs out behind it. Quinn holds the Selkie into the sea.
barrels.clue: The sun is still high, and two yellow barrels ride in the wake.
barrels.prompt: Hoy has thrown two barrels over the side ___.
barrels.explanation: THIS MORNING is not finished, so the Present Perfect fits. AT SIX is a finished point, and AGO always takes the Past Simple.

last.title: THE FOURTH BARREL GOES
last.story: The line tears out over the rail. Quinn holds the wheel. The kraken takes the fourth barrel under.
last.clue: The harpoon line runs off the drum. That was the fourth and last barrel.
last.prompt: What do you say into the radio at last?

answers.text: We have been fixing four barrels to it.
We have fixed four barrels to it now.
We have fixing four barrels to it now.

last.explanation: A number is a result, and a result takes HAVE + PAST PARTICIPLE. The Present Perfect Continuous counts time, not totals, and needs BEEN.

hotspot.object: the channel marker where the water splits

sound.title: WHERE THE WATER SPLITS
sound.story: Past the harbour mouth the channel divides. Hoy has the sonar ready. Choose where you search first.

choices.label: RUN FOR THE REEF
choices.note: Open water over the reef, where the creel boats set their nets.

choices.label: ENTER THE SEA CAVES
choices.note: Low water opens the cave mouths. The Selkie anchors off and waits.

decision.title: RUN OR STAY
decision.story: The tide turns at midnight. Quinn wants the Corry. Baird wants the regatta lights on. Choose tonight.

choices.label: RUN FOR THE WHIRLPOOL
choices.note: Quinn knows the slack water. The whirlpool is the kraken's ground.

choices.label: HOLD THE HARBOUR TONIGHT
choices.note: Two hundred people ashore, and the whole fleet moored and lit.

master.label: PRESENT PERFECT MASTER
master.title: THE FLEET GOES OUT
master.text: Four barrels held. The black tide has gone out of the loch. Quinn ties the Selkie up himself. At noon Baird sends the fleet out, and Kilmara works the Sound again.

complete.label: KRAKEN GONE
complete.title: QUINN COMES ASHORE ALIVE
complete.text: The barrels come up. The thing under them does not. Quinn sits on the slip, wet and alive. What is left of the Selkie lies beside him. By evening the loch is quiet.

missing.label: BARRELS MISSING
missing.title: IT GOES DOWN UNMARKED
missing.text: You did not get four barrels into it. The black tide slides back into the Corry with nothing to follow. No skipper will leave the pier while it is down there. Read the chart again and take the boat out.

failed.label: OUT OF CHANCES
failed.title: THE SELKIE IS NOT BACK
failed.text: The berth where the Selkie ties up is empty water. The lifeboat has been out since dark, and nobody has found anything. At first light nobody else will go out. The story is not over.
